newsitem.title: JAPAN: Japan carmakers may hold back exports in 1997.
newsitem.headline: Japan carmakers may hold back exports in 1997.

text.p: Japan's vehicle exports are expected to fall next year as carmakers curb shipments to avoid trade friction with the United States, analysts said Thursday.
The comments came after an industry body said Japan's vehicle exports rose 14.1 percent in November from a year earlier to 329,868 vehicles, the sixth successive month of year-on-year gains.

"Japan's top makers will curb their exports to the United States in the latter half of next year to avoid trade friction with the United States and to adjust inventories there," said Noriyuki Matsushima, a senior analyst at Nikko Research.

"Toyota and Honda are sensitive about increased exports to the United States. Japan's vehicle exports in calendar 1997 are likely to fall to 3.59 million vehicles," said Seiji Sugiura, a Nomura Research analyst.

Exports for 1996 of a predicted 3.73 million vehicles would also be down from last year, said the Japan Automobile Manufacturers' Association, but there is still pressure on the carmakers to hold back exports because of rapid increases in exports in the last six months.
The association also announced on Thursday that Japanese vehicle makers bought a record $10.89 billion worth of U.S. car parts and materials in the six months to September 30.
The previous record for a six-month period was $10.70 billion for the second half of the 1995-96 fiscal year, which ended on March 31.
The figure was also 5.5 percent higher than the $10.33 billion in purchases in the first half of the 1995/96 year.
The 1996-97, half-year purchase comprised $9.20 billion worth of parts for use at the carmakers' American units and $1.69 billion for imports into Japan.
The association said Japanese carmakers bought $2.76 billion worth of car parts and materials made in the European Union in the April-September period.
